title: Installing software: installers, stores and package managers

videos.script: The accountant needs a program to open a client's compressed files, and asks Ana to install it. The quickest way is to search for its name, click the first result and run whatever downloads. It is also how a large share of the malware on office computers arrives, from a page that looks like the real one and a file that is almost the real one. {{search}} Every system now offers something better: a place that has already checked the program, installs it with one action, keeps it updated with everything else, and removes it cleanly. On Linux that place is the package manager, and it has been the normal way for thirty years. Windows and macOS have stores, and each has a package manager of its own too. {{better}} The difference that matters is not convenience. It is who has checked what you are about to run with your permissions, and who will fix it when a flaw is found next year. {{trust}} In this lesson you will install a program with apt and see exactly what it put where, watch it bring the other packages a program needs, remove them without leaving debris, and read the record of what was done. Then the same jobs on Windows, with winget and installers, and on macOS, with the App Store, disk images and Homebrew. {{steps}} The Linux transcripts come from lesson 3's server. The Windows and macOS commands are shown, not run. {{honest}}
